subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should OpenClaw solve #41484 as narrow per-job and heartbeat elevated authority markers, or fold the elevated-exec requirement into the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design while keeping heartbeat provenance in scope?
rationale: This choice defines when autonomous cron and heartbeat turns may inherit host-elevated exec authority and affects persisted cron/API shape, heartbeat config semantics, migration, audit, and compatibility.

options.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
options.body: Treat #41484 as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader schedule provenance model while explicitly preserving heartbeat provenance as a required design point.

options.title: Implement Narrow Elevated Markers
options.body: Add per-job and heartbeat-modifier elevated approval state now, with focused create, update, execution, migration, audit, and docs coverage.

options.title: Fail Closed For Internal Sources
options.body: Remove cron-event and heartbeat wildcard elevation only if maintainers accept a compatibility-breaking hardening step and provide an upgrade story.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
recommendation.body: Treat #41484 as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader schedule provenance model while explicitly preserving heartbeat provenance as a required design point.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent agent cron caller-scope PR makes this the closest current owner path for scheduling provenance decisions.
